articles.title: Apple’s OLED iPad Mini upgrade is on the way as prices continue to rise
articles.summary: Apple is reportedly planning to upgrade the iPad Mini with an OLED display later this year, but it will likely come with another price increase.
articles.body: The iPad Mini could get an OLED display upgrade as soon as October, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. It would be the most significant refresh for the Mini since its 2021 redesign. An OLED iPad Mini has been rumored for months now, with Gurman previously reporting last year that it will also come with a price increase, and earlier this week he said the price of AppleCare Plus for Macs and iPads is going up. That iPad Mini price hike is even more likely now after Apple raised prices across its product lineup last month — including the current iPad Mini, which now costs $100 more. According to Tim Cook, the price hikes were in response to the ongoing RAM shortage, which could last for years, so the OLED iPad Mini will almost certainly be even pricier than its predecessor. In addition to the OLED iPad Mini, Gurman says Apple is planning upgrades to the iPad Air and the base iPad, slated for early next year. The base iPad will reportedly get a relatively minor refresh with an updated processor but no major design changes. Gurman says Apple is planning an “eventual OLED upgrade for the iPad Air,” with earlier rumors pointing to that upgrade coming sometime next year. According to Gurman, iPad Pro and Apple Pencil updates could also arrive this coming spring.

articles.title: Why Apple is finally making its own smart home devices
articles.summary: Apple’s new smart home lineup promises easier setup, tighter integration, and data privacy. But with steep competition and steeper prices, can Apple convince more people to adopt its vision of the smart home?
articles.body: For more than a decade, Apple has told other companies to build smart home devices for its platform. This week, Apple launched its own. The Apple Home Collection is a lineup of cameras, thermostats, sensors, a smart door lock, and a video doorbell, all codeveloped with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. They arrive alongside HomeView, Apple’s first smart display. Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still feels underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition. Amazon’s and Google’s ecosystems support more products, and both have popular in-house brands: Ring and Nest. Apple had nothing of its own to point customers to as an Apple experience — and now it does. But why now? And does Apple actually add anything new here, or is this mostly packaging? At Apple’s “Welcome home” event in New York this week, I spoke with Kaiann Drance, vice president of product marketing for home at Apple, about the company’s new approach to the smart home and what this means for Apple’s commitment to Matter, the interoperable open smart home standard it helped found. [Image: Apple’s HomeView is viewed as a gateway to bring people into the smart home. Why now? Drance says the big reason was the development of the right technologies. The first was Matter, which provided the ecosystem. The second was AI, which brought a more conversational Siri voice assistant. Both were necessary to create a dedicated home device in HomeView. “With the magic of Siri AI, it comes together in a way that we haven’t been able to deliver before,” Drance says. “That’s been a really critical piece of bringing this all together.” The bigger play here is HomeView as a gateway to the smart home for Apple’s users. Buy one for playing music, guided cooking recipes, and checking your calendar, and you might soon want a camera or smart lock to go with it. Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do. She’s not wrong. The biggest barrier to buying smart devices is that people don’t see any value in the products, according to research from Parks Associates. Privacy and security concerns and complexity also rank high, along with cost. While Apple isn’t addressing the cost concern here — the products start at $200 — the other elements are part of its pitch: one-tap setup, your data stays yours, one app to run it all. Apple’s stamp of approval also carries a lot of weight. “People who own Apple products are very, very loyal, and there is a large user base,” says Elizabeth Parks, president and CMO at Parks Associates. [Image: Several Apple Home Collection products: LG smart door lock, indoor camera and video doorbell, and a Schneider Electric thermostat. From a choose-your-own adventure to a tailored solution Until now, Apple Home has been a bit like a buffet: You can pick from any brand that supports HomeKit or Matter and hope it all goes together. The Home Collection is more like the chef’s choice, a short list of dishes Apple promises will pair well. Drance says that’s what some customers were asking for. “There is a lot of choice with Matter, and there’s a lot of great products out there,” she says. “But sometimes we do get asked, ‘Hey, what product should I put in the home?’” Rather than build devices itself, Apple chose to codevelop the lineup with partners that “have their own expertise in the home.” Both have a global footprint and home experience, she says, “LG more so in consumer products, Schneider through home build and home installations.” Drance says it was a ground-up collaboration with Apple bringing “the design aesthetic that would be suitable for the home and suitable to go with our family of products.” The company is also partnering with ADT through Apple retail stores to help people install the devices. Drance says setup and ease of use were a big focus. “The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app,” she says. “We just wanted that simplicity to be at its core, and of course, the privacy that we’ve developed together with our partners.” She says everything integrates through Apple Home; you don’t need to create an LG or Schneider account, and all data is end-to-end encrypted, so only you can access it. Drance was clear that the Apple Home Collection isn’t replacing the buffet — the hardware ecosystem that has grown up around Apple Home. “We still have this incredible ecosystem with Matter, and with Works with Apple Home, that is going to remain,” she says. “We know that homes are not a one-size-fits-all solution, so our customers will continue to have that choice, and we remain committed to building that ecosystem as well.” The hardware mostly backs that up. The lock, thermostats, and sensors are Matter-compatible; the lock supports Aliro and works entirely locally, and every device supports Thread. The exception is the cameras, which use Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video, not Matter. That’s the biggest lock-in. I was surprised Apple didn’t announce Matter camera support. But the Thread radios suggest the hardware might be Matter-ready, and Apple may be waiting for the Matter camera standard to support encrypted uploads, something HKSV already does. So, what’s the benefit? Does the Home Collection do anything other Apple Home devices can’t? In theory, no; in practice, yes. “What we’ve done with Apple Home Collection is we’ve added another layer on top of that, that deeper integration,” says Drance. There aren’t features exclusive to the Home Collection; it’s more that Apple is saying all the features will be here. It’s a bit like Google making a Pixel phone to show Android developers what Android can do: Apple’s products come with the full suite of capabilities the platform offers. "“The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app.”" - Kaiann Drance, Apple According to Apple, setup is as simple as tapping your iPhone to the device, like pairing AirPods, with no extra account or app needed and no scanning required. Every device uses Thread to stay connected if Wi-Fi drops, and Apple says each can update its own network credentials when you change your Wi-Fi. This could address the offline-device problems that plague Apple Home. Everything is end-to-end encrypted, and the cameras keep recording to onboard storage if your Wi-Fi drops. The devices also support Apple Home features other manufacturers have been slow to adopt. The LG lock is only the third to offer hands-free Home Key unlocking over UWB, and both thermostats work with Apple’s Clean Energy Guidance and Adaptive Temperature, which adjusts around your location and sleep schedule. At least that’s the promise. We’ll have to test these devices to see how well they deliver. [Image: The LG door lock and video doorbell pair in the Apple Home app so you can unlock the door when you see who is at the door. A curated garden path Together, Apple’s new devices form a polished, cohesive starter kit for the smart home — albeit an expensive one. The cameras, lock, and thermostats cost $200 to $400, and camera history requires an iCloud Plus plan. As Drance said, the smart home isn’t a one-size-fits-all solution, so this won’t work for everybody. If you already have a Ring doorbell or Google Nest Hub, this probably isn’t for you. Instead, Apple is trying to guide its existing customers who haven’t bought a video doorbell or smart lock yet down a curated path into the smart home. However, Apple faces a tougher challenge in the broader market: It’s arriving late. The smart display category is already mature; millions of homes have Echo and Google smart displays. Millions more have Ring or Nest doorbells, neither of which will work with HomeView at launch. As a smart home platform, Apple Home ranks third in adoption, behind Google, with Amazon holding a big lead, according to Parks Associates research. But customer loyalty to those platforms isn’t guaranteed. Four in five smart-home households would consider switching, Parks says, especially if another platform lets them control everything in one place. “Interoperability will be critical, but the bigger prize is owning the consumer relationship,” she says. With its Home Collection, Apple isn’t reinventing the smart home; it’s trying to make it easier to get into one.

articles.title: Todd Chrisley and wife Julie hit with $1.57 million IRS tax lien after Donald Trump’s 2025 pardon; claims involve 2021 and 2022 taxes, separate from couple’s $36 million bank fraud and tax evasion case
articles.summary: Reality TV personalities Todd Chrisley and wife Julie are facing renewed financial scrutiny after the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) filed a federal tax
articles.body: Reality TV personalities Todd Chrisley and wife Julie are facing renewed financial scrutiny after the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) filed a federal tax lien of approximately $1.57 million against them in Davidson County, Tennessee. The development comes more than a year after US President Donald Trump granted the couple a presidential pardon in connection with their high-profile federal fraud and tax evasion convictions.According to Page Six, which reported the development after reviewing public records, the lien was filed on August 19, 2026. The assessments relate to unpaid taxes for two separate periods, covering 2021 and 2022.The new tax development has drawn attention because the couple’s earlier convictions had resulted in prison sentences before Trump’s intervention in May 2025. However, the reported lien concerns tax assessments that are separate from the criminal case for which they received pardons.Todd and Julie Chrisley’s $1.57 million IRS tax lien explainedAccording to records reviewed by Page Six, the federal tax lien comprises two assessments.The first is for $142,410.72 for the tax period ending December 31, 2021. The assessment was reportedly made on December 5, 2022.The second, substantially larger assessment amounts to $1,429,041.89 for the tax period ending December 31, 2022. It was reportedly assessed on December 11, 2023.Together, the two assessments total approximately $1.57 million.The lien was filed in Davidson County, Tennessee, on August 19, 2026. The report states that it is unrelated to the financial transactions underlying Todd and Julie’s earlier federal convictions.A tax lien is a legal claim against property arising from unpaid tax obligations. Its filing does not, by itself, establish that the couple have committed a new criminal offence.Why Donald Trump pardoned Todd and Julie Chrisley in 2025Todd and Julie Chrisley were convicted in June 2022 in a federal case involving bank fraud and tax evasion. Prosecutors alleged that the couple obtained more than $36 million in loans by submitting falsified financial documents to lenders.According to prosecutors, the money was used to finance an expensive lifestyle that included vehicles, designer clothing, homes and travel.The couple were sentenced to a combined 19 years in prison and began serving their sentences in January 2023. Todd, now 57, initially received a 12-year sentence, which was subsequently reduced to 10 years. Julie, now 53, was sentenced to seven years.Todd served his sentence in Florida, while Julie was incarcerated in Kentucky.In May 2025, Trump pardoned the couple, bringing their imprisonment to an end. Their daughter Savannah Chrisley had publicly campaigned for their release, and the president reportedly called her personally to inform her of his decision.The pardon addressed their federal criminal convictions. It should not be interpreted as automatically cancelling separate tax assessments or other financial obligations.Todd Chrisley previously denied remorse over his convictionFollowing his release, Todd publicly challenged the circumstances surrounding his conviction.During a 2025 news conference, he was asked whether he felt remorse for the conduct that had led to his conviction.“I would have remorse if it was something that I did,” he said, adding that he believed alleged corruption in the case would continue to come to light.His remarks reflected his continued opposition to the prosecution’s account of the events. The new tax lien, however, is a separate matter and does not by itself resolve disputes over the original case.Todd and Julie Chrisley return to television after their releaseDespite the legal and financial scrutiny surrounding their case, the Chrisleys have continued making television appearances.Earlier in 2026, the couple appeared on Fox’s reality competition series The Masked Singer, performing Elvis Presley’s “Jailhouse Rock” in a playful reference to their prison sentences.Todd told Gold Derby that he had wanted to perform the song as a tongue-in-cheek response to their circumstances and their critics.Julie said the experience had been enjoyable despite taking her outside her comfort zone, explaining that she was not a singer but had loved competing alongside her husband.Their appearance marked another chapter in the couple’s efforts to remain in the public eye following their release.Savannah Chrisley and the family’s role in their releaseSavannah played a prominent role in campaigning for her parents’ freedom before Trump granted their pardons.Todd is the father of five children. He shares daughter Lindsie and son Kyle with his former wife, Teresa Terry. With Julie, he has children Chase, Savannah and Grayson.The family’s public profile grew through the reality series Chrisley Knows Best, which followed their affluent lifestyle and family relationships.Their criminal convictions and subsequent pardons became a major turning point in their public story, bringing their financial dealings under renewed scrutiny.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: Ellen DeGeneres plots TV comeback 4 years after controversial exit
articles.summary: Nearly five years after 'The Ellen DeGeneres Show' ended amid allegations of a toxic workplace, the former talk show host is plotting her next move.
articles.body:
Ellen DeGeneres still has TV on the brain.

Nearly five years after "The Ellen DeGeneres Show" ended amid allegations of a toxic workplace , DeGeneres, 68, revealed during an Oct. 16 appearance on "The Graham Norton Show" that she misses the limelight.

"I've nothing really going on and I really miss being on TV," said DeGeneres, who moved to the United Kingdom with her wife, Portia de Rossi, in 2024. "I miss a lot about it – laughing with the writers and the audience. I think about doing stuff here."

DeGeneres jokingly added: "I think it is pretty easy to get on TV here."

DeGeneres' contract officially expired in May 2022, two years after current and former employees alleged in a Buzzfeed News report that they experienced racism, fear and intimidation while working on the show. DeGeneres later issued a public apology on the air.

In a statement to USA TODAY in 2020, executive producers Ed Glavin, Mary Connelly and Andy Lassner said they were "truly heartbroken and sorry to learn" about the claims. Glavin, executive producer Kevin Leman and co-executive producer Jonathan Norman were ousted from the syndicated talk show the following month.

"You have a pottery show, you have a sewing show, and you even have a show about people watching TV shows," DeGeneres said, referencing U.K. TV shows "The Great Pottery Throwdown," "The Great British Sewing Bee" and "Gogglebox."

DeGeneres embarked on a stand-up tour after the show ended but canceled several dates before releasing a Netflix special in which she told fans it was "the last time you're going to see me."

Ellen DeGeneres is looking for 'something' to do

DeGeneres admitted to BBC in a July 2025 interview that while she loved her new, relaxing life in the English countryside, she had grown "a little bit bored."

"I want to have fun. I want to do something. I do like my chickens..." she said. DeGeneres announced in April that she would reprise her role as Dory in a new short set in the "Finding Nemo" universe.

"Excited about this," she wrote in an April 24 Instagram post. While DeGeneres might have been excited by the prospect of getting back out there, she told the outlet she's not sure she could run another show the same way.

"I just feel like people are watching on their phones, or people aren't really paying attention as much to televisions, because we're so inundated with information and entertainment," DeGeneres said.

In any case, she's planning her comeback "very carefully."

articles.title: Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
articles.summary: Apple’s App Store rules now more explicitly ban so-called “nudify” apps that generate intimate images of people without their consent using AI tools, including “bait-and-switch” apps with “nudification” features.
articles.body: Apple’s App Store rules now more explicitly ban so-called “nudify” apps that generate intimate images of people without their consent using AI tools. The rule changes follow significant criticism toward Apple after X users used Grok earlier this year to make nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes, including minors. Apple didn’t pull X or Grok from the App Store, though it told senators that it threatened to yank Grok. At Apple’s WWDC event in June, protestors also called on Apple to “remove Grok, X, and all nudify technology from the App Store,” and in July, a San Francisco city attorney ordered Apple to remove 13 “nudify” apps, which it said it did. As part of updates announced Friday, Apple says that developers “must proactively prevent and remove” nonconsensual, sexual images as part of its content moderation requirements for App Store apps. Developers who “fail to implement adequate safeguards” or “don’t remedy violations after notice” may be removed from the App Store. Apple also clarified a rule that bars “bait-and-switch” apps, or apps that add or change features, including “nudification,” after they have been approved. Apple’s rules also more clearly spell out that any apps that “facilitate human trafficking or the exploitation of children” will be pulled from the App Store and “blocked from alternative distribution.”

articles.title: All the news about the iPhone Duo
articles.summary: Apple’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, goes on sale on October 23rd. Here’s all of our coverage.
articles.body: Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo. The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease. Instead of Face ID, it uses Touch ID on the power button. It has two cameras, a main lens and a wide-angle lens. Apple completely revamped iOS 27’s controls and apps for the foldable, including putting the dock on the side of the phone. And it has a flashy opening animation when you unfold the phone. The iPhone Duo a big new bet from Apple, though one that’s a little late to the game compared to competitors like Samsung and Google. The phone isn’t cheap: it starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, and the prices only go up from there. Still, Apple said that preorder demand was “extraordinary,” so it could have a hit on its hands. Here’s everything unfolding about the iPhone Duo.

articles.title: College Football Playoff expanding again, but the money behind it is not what some would call a 'win'
articles.summary: College football playoff expansion to 24 teams moves closer as ESPN and the CFP informally agree to a $345 million figure for additional games
articles.body: Expansion of the College Football Playoff only needs a few approval signatures and final votes before we can officially start discussing what the sport will look like moving forward now that monetary figures are being finalized. Over the past month, college football commissioners have been dissecting what the financial terms would look like once ESPN presented its final offer for the next iteration of the postseason tournament to crown a national champion. According to sources familiar with the ongoing negotiations, ESPN and the CFP have informally agreed to a contract that would see the network pay an additional $345 million annually for the rights to eleven more football games that would take place with the 24-team playoff. COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF EXPANSION IS NOTHING MORE THAN A DESPERATE FINANCIAL BAILOUT DISGUISED AS PROGRESS ESPN was first to report the financial details of its offer to the CFP, which would eliminate conference championship games after this season. Over the next five years, with the loss of conference championship games, the network would pay for those leagues to get out of marketing agreements, along with the revenue generated from those same conference title weekends. ESPN will have to pay FOX upwards of $60 million annually for the Big Ten to exit its agreement with the network, sources added. THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF IS SACRIFICING ITS SOUL TO BE AN ATM FOR CONFERENCES WITH EXPANSION TO 24 TEAMS A lot can change in just three years for college football Just three years ago, CFP committee members agreed to increase the amount of teams from four to twelve, in what many around the sport thought was a pretty decent tradeoff if the postseason was going to expand. At that time, the thought of a 24-team playoff would have been laughed at, and was behind closed doors across college campuses. But, thanks to the increased spending across college sports related to revenue-sharing and NIL budgets, along with a plethora of power-four schools operating at a deficit, there was chatter that sometime in the near future that number would only rise again. Look no further than the NCAA Tournament, which recently expanded from 68 to 76 teams, as an example of college athletics looking to add more schools to an already crowded field. Now, after over a year of back-and-forth negotiating by conferences on what the right amount of teams should be if the CFP were to have expanded, that number increases by twelve. If you remember back to last year's conversation, the thought was that if college football was going to add more teams, that number could have just reached sixteen, thanks to a hard push by the SEC. GREG SANKEY MAKES IT CLEAR THAT SEC DIDN’T START THE 16-TEAM CFP FORMAT DISCUSSION, THAT'S ON THE BIG TEN At the same time, it was the Big Ten conference that held steady in its convictions that having a 24-team field would be the right move, giving more schools an opportunity to fight for the championship. More teams will make the college football postseason better, right? In reality, the additional twelve teams added a a justification mechanism to the postseason, given how many schools are spending over $30 million per year just to piece together a roster good enough to contend for a playoff spot. So, with a push from Big Ten Commissioner Tony Petitti, other conferences, including the ACC and Big 12, embraced the idea that a 24-team postseason would give their teams more opportunities to play meaningful football in December while creating a simpler path to the playoff. articles.title: Rise and Fall 2: Raj Grover breaks silence on being called Siwet Tomar and Priyanka Chahar Choudhary’s ‘chamcha’, addresses Gautam Gulati’s bullying claims
articles.summary: Raj Grover, who was recently evicted from Rise and Fall 2, has opened up about his journey on the reality show, addressing the criticism he faced over his
articles.body: Raj Grover, who was recently evicted from Rise and Fall 2, has opened up about his journey on the reality show, addressing the criticism he faced over his friendships with Siwet Tomar and Priyanka Chahar Choudhary. He also spoke about the audience’s allegations of Gautam Gulati bullying him during his stint on the show.Taking to his Instagram handle, Raj shared a video reflecting on his experience and clarifying his side of the story. Addressing the criticism he received during the first week, Raj recalled how viewers called him Siwet’s ‘chamcha’ because of their friendship. However, he maintained that Siwet never influenced his decisions.“I was with him like a very good friend, but there was not a single place where he influenced my decision,” Raj said.“When we do not even know what is going to happen next, then how can someone give me names all of a sudden?” he questioned, adding that his friendship with Siwet did not mean he was blindly following him.Raj also addressed being called Priyanka Chahar Choudhary’s ‘chamcha’. Explaining his perspective, he said that contestants who spend almost 24 hours together are bound to develop friendships.“When you’re with those six people for 24 hours, someone will become your friend, you’ll talk to someone, right?” he said.Raj added that the age difference between him and the other contestants might have contributed to how viewers perceived his relationships. He also suggested that Priyanka’s more vocal personality made it appear as though he was always listening to her. “I’m being very honest, 90% of the time I was the one giving advice to Priyanka as well,” he claimed.He further explained that he had watched the previous season carefully and had his own strategies for the game. “I had a lot of strategies in my mind, which I used to give,” Raj said, maintaining that his friendship with Priyanka was mutual and did not mean he lacked an independent approach to the game.Raj also addressed viewers’ reactions to his equation with Gautam Gulati. Explaining why he did not always react strongly to Gautam’s behaviour, he said he viewed their relationship much like his bond with his elder siblings.“In real life, I have an elder sister and an elder brother; they trouble me a lot,” he said, explaining that he generally avoids reacting aggressively or disrespecting them.“That’s reality TV. You can’t compare it to real life. You can’t give him real-life treatment,” he said, suggesting that situations on a reality show are often expected to be portrayed more dramatically.Reflecting on his eviction, Raj also spoke about the support he received from viewers. He recalled receiving numerous comments and direct messages on his and his family’s social media accounts from people who claimed to have voted for him every day.“We voted for you every day, brother. We’re voting every day, we’re supporting you every day,” he recalled viewers telling him.He admitted that the messages made him question the voting outcome. “Somewhere, I can’t quite believe that I was behind anyone in the voting,” Raj said. However, he added that he did not want to dwell on the issue, saying, “But leave it, let’s not victimize that.”Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Chuck Lorre claims Cybill Shepherd became ‘a different person’ when shooting season 2 of “Cybill”
articles.summary: The future creator of “The Big Bang Theory” writes about his Hollywood career in his new memoir.
articles.body:
TV producer and writer Chuck Lorre wrote about his time on the '90s sitcom Cybill in his new book.

He recalled leaving the set, even though he was told not to, during an argument.

Trouble began, he alleged, in the second season after Cybill Shepherd "became a different person."

Chuck Lorre recounts in his new book that working on the sitcom Cybill wasn't always a laugh.

Lorre created the series that centered around actress Cybill Shepherd, who was known for TV's Moonlighting and movies such as The Last Picture Show and Taxi Driver .

Cybill debuted in 1995, six years after her hit with Bruce Willis ended. The story of a struggling, middle-aged actress that costarred Christine Baranski, Alicia Witt, and Alan Rosenberg was a hit.

"When season two began, in keeping with her name, Cybill became a different person," Lorre, the showrunner, wrote in his new book, Sitcom: A Memoir . "She made her toady manager a co-­ exec, and angrily demanded complete control of the stories, scripts, casting, cameras, lighting, editing, and probably craft services."

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

As he remembered, the scrutiny didn't stop there.

"After every table read and rehearsal," Lorre wrote, "I would be ordered to her trailer, where I had to sit on a footstool while she gave me script notes, enthroned in one of those giant leather vibrating Sharper Image lounge chairs."

While the Emmy-winning series continued to air new episodes until 1998, Lorre didn't last as its leader.

He wrote that, just before his firing in the second season, he "was told the Queen of Mirth was unhappy with act two of the script in production. I probably had a few drinks to fortify my courage, then informed all concerned that there was nothing wrong with act two, and that I was going home. I was warned not to. But I did."

There were consequences — and they came swiftly.

"Later that night, Yom Kippur eve, I got a call from a low-­ level exec at Carsey-­ Werner informing me not to come back. I was fired. (The Arabs always attack on a Jewish holiday)," Lorre wrote. "Someone would clear out my office and send everything to my home."

Entertainment Weekly has reached out to a rep for Shepherd.

As for Lorre, his career in television was far from over.

He went on to create big hits, such as Two and a Half Men , The Big Bang Theory , and Mom .

Shepherd has alleged that her sitcom was ultimately canceled after she refused the sexual advances of CBS executive Les Moonves, who was forced out of the network in 2018 following multiple sexual misconduct allegations, which he denied.

"It would have run another five years," she said in December 2018 on SiriusXM's The Michelle Collins Show . "We had the best writers in the world, and directors and actors — everybody was brilliant."

Lorre writes about his adventures in Hollywood in Sitcom: A Memoir , available in bookstores now.

articles.title: Ember’s new temperature-controlled mug makes my nightly tea ritual even better | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The biggest change about Ember's new mug is that you no longer have to open the app to adjust your drink’s temperature.
articles.body:
With the nights getting chillier, I’ve been reaching for a cup of tea more often. And if there’s one thing that can make a cozy fall night even better, it’s a warm drink that actually stays warm. Enter Ember’s new Mug 3 , the latest version of the company’s temperature-controlled smart mug, which is designed to keep your drink at just the right temperature for as long as you sip.

Ember first introduced its smart mug in 2016 to solve a problem most coffee and tea drinkers know all too well: getting distracted for a few minutes, only to return to a lukewarm drink. Now, the company is back with its third-generation mug, which brings a handful of practical upgrades.

The biggest change is that you no longer have to open the app to adjust your drink’s temperature. Instead, you can use the button on the bottom of the mug to cycle through five preset temperatures, starting at 125 degrees Fahrenheit. Each press raises the temperature by five degrees, up to a maximum of 145 degrees, so you can easily make your drink a little hotter with each click.

Honestly, this is the feature I ended up using the most during my time testing out the mug. At night, when I’m curled up in bed with a book and a cup of tea, my phone is usually somewhere across the room. Being able to adjust my drink without getting up to find it is a small convenience, but one I genuinely appreciate.

It’s also a welcome change for users who have reported running into connectivity or pairing issues with the Ember app.

That said, I do have one complaint: the button is located on the bottom of the mug. It’s a peculiar design choice when you’re dealing with a cup full of hot liquid, and it isn’t particularly easy to press, either. I often found myself tilting the mug and pressing down firmly to get it to respond. So, while I appreciate the addition of on-mug controls, I wish Ember had made the button easier to reach.

If you prefer using your phone, the Ember app still offers plenty of customization. After pairing the mug with your phone over Bluetooth, you can choose presets based on what you’re drinking. Ember recommends 136 degrees Fahrenheit for black coffee, 132 degrees for green tea, and 142 degrees for lemon water. You can also create your own temperature presets, which is handy if you like your drinks a little hotter or cooler than the recommended settings.

The Mug 3 also comes with a few other upgrades, including a sliding lid designed to help prevent spills. The mug can also keep your drink at its desired temperature for up to three hours on a single charge. And it’s the first mug in Ember’s lineup to be top-rack dishwasher-safe, making cleanup easier. (Just keep in mind that it isn’t microwave-safe.)

The Ember Mug 3 comes in two sizes: a 10-ounce model for $129 and a 14-ounce version for $149.

The smaller mug is available in black, white, and stainless steel, while the larger size comes in eight colors, including sage green, lavender, powder blue, salt blue, sandstone, white, black, and matcha green.

Alongside the new mug, Ember also introduced the Tumbler 2 , which replaces both the Travel Mug 2 and the original Tumbler in its lineup. The 16-ounce tumbler features a slimmer, taller design intended to fit standard car cup holders. It’s available in black for $179, while the Travel Mug 2 will remain available until supplies run out.

The products are available to purchase on Ember’s website, Target, and Amazon.

articles.title: Mercedes-AMG’s first ground-up SUV is a 1,150hp electric beast
articles.summary: Mercedes-AMG announced the new GT SUV, its first electric SUV built in-house, from the ground up.
articles.body: Earlier this year, Mercedes’ AMG performance brand grabbed our attention with the GT four-door coupe, a souped-up sports sedan with three axial flux motors delivering over 1,150 horsepower. Well, now meet its beefier cousin, the 2028 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV, an equally powerful, ultra-fast-charging electric people-hauler. The AMG GT SUV (say that five times fast) marks the first time in the performance brand’s 59-year history that it has developed a full-size SUV entirely in-house from the ground up. Scheduled to hit the US next summer, the new EV is built on Merc’s high-performance AMG.EA architecture to combine sports-car handling with full-size SUV suburban practicality. It will be available in three trims — GT 53, GT 55, and the flagship GT 63 — with the top model delivering 1,153hp via the same three axial flux motors powering the four-door coupe. That beats the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric with Launch Control, which is sure to make for some awkward run-ins around Stuttgart. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Thanks to an 800-volt architecture, the SUV supports blistering-fast charging speeds up to 710kW on the 128kWh battery (GT 63 / GT 55) and 600kW on the 106kWh battery (GT 53). Drivers can charge 10–80 percent in 12 minutes or gain up to 450km (around 280 miles) of WLTP range in just 10 minutes. The 128kWh battery trims will have an estimated max range of 435 miles. That battery, by the way? It utilizes F1-inspired technology with specialized NCMA cathodes, silicon-containing anodes, and cylindrical cells. An electrically nonconductive oil flows directly around each individual cell for uniform thermal management, enabling continuous high-power delivery and long battery life. Mercedes has quietly been on the vanguard of battery technology for a while now, with the AMG GT SUV just the latest example. The 710kW charging speed, in particular, could give Mercedes another edge over Porsche’s 320kW speeds. For a full-size SUV, the AMG GT sounds like it could handle like a vehicle half its size. Mercedes-AMG replaced the traditional mechanical roll bars with a newly developed suspension that uses active hydraulic elements to eliminate pitch and roll during acceleration, heavy braking, and cornering. Combined with three-stage air springs and standard six-degree active rear-axle steering, it purports to balance track precision with long-distance comfort. But just because it’s a beefy lad doesn’t mean it’ll tip the scales. The AMG GT 63 SUV weighs in at 5,941lbs, making it slightly lighter than the Lotus Eletre R (6,007lbs) and Lucid Gravity (6,100lbs), and nearly identical to the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric (5,960lbs). [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Silence is golden — except to a performance brand’s EV engineering team. That means piping in recorded sounds of real AMGs — in this case, the legendary AMG V8 and six-cylinder engines — to preserve the “emotional” AMG identity. Mercedes is proud that it’s using real engine sounds over synthetic EV tones, though some may disagree. The system even simulates mechanical gear shifts with paddle controls, offers adjustable sound profiles, and integrates physical seat vibrations — so you can still feel like there’s a real engine under that hood instead of a 78-liter frunk. The so-called AMGFORCE Sport+ drive program is offered as standard across all three trims of the Mercedes-AMG GT SUV. Inside, you’ll find the MB.OS platform on your 14-inch display, with an army of AI agents from ChatGPT, Microsoft, and Google at your disposal to boss around. Use them to set navigation, discover random locations, do web searches, tell bad jokes, or whatever else people use AI for in their cars. Merc’s own onboard AI system can handle the physical stuff, like adjusting HVAC, changing drive modes, or fiddling with the lighting — all through voice commands. [Image: Beyond voice and navigation, the AMG GT SUV applies AI to high-performance track driving through something called the Predictive Performance Manager. Mercedes says the PPM uses track-mapping data to dynamically throttle or boost electric motor output depending on topography, conserving battery energy on downhill or technical winding sections so full power is available on steep inclines and long straights. That could also mean faster, more consistent overall lap times by eliminating battery overheating and power throttling during track driving — something an AMG lover would likely appreciate. Mercedes didn’t release the official pricing yet, though we can expect something closer to its official launch.

articles.title: Here's some tips on how to organize photos with keywords on your phone
articles.summary: Apple's iOS 27 lets you add keywords to iPhone photos, while Samsung Gallery tags and Google Photos search offer similar organization tools.
articles.body: Your phone probably holds thousands of pictures. Some are important family memories, while others are screenshots you saved because you thought you might need them later. Then comes the frustrating part. You remember taking a particular photo, but finding it feels like searching for a needle in a digital haystack. Apple's iOS 27 offers a way to make that search easier by letting you add keywords to individual photos. Instead of scrolling through months of pictures, you can search for a word you've assigned to a photo and pull it up again. Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel users have similar ways to organize their pictures, although the tools work differently. Here's how to take advantage of them and spend less time hunting for photos. Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com. YOUR PHONE CAN FIX BADLY FRAMED PHOTOS AFTER YOU TAKE THEM How to add keywords to photos on iPhone Apple's Photos app can already recognize people, pets, places and objects. However, automatic searches don't always understand why a particular photo is important to you. That's where manually assigned keywords can help. For example, you might photograph a parking spot at an airport or save a picture of a particular appliance model number. Adding a keyword you will remember later can make the photo much easier to find. Add keywords to photos in iOS 27 These instructions are based on an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 27. Choose words that make sense to you. For example, a picture of your car's license plate might get a keyword such as "license plate." You could also tag pictures from a family vacation with a memorable trip name. How to find photos using keywords on iPhone Once you've added keywords, searching for those pictures takes only a few seconds. You can also manage your keywords by opening Photos > Collections > your profile icon > Manage Keywords. From there, you can rename keywords, delete them or add frequently used keywords to your favorites. Pro tip: Start with photos you actually struggle to find. Important documents, appliance labels and travel information are useful candidates. There's no need to spend an entire weekend tagging your photo library. How to organize photos on Samsung Galaxy Samsung Galaxy phones also let you add tags to pictures using the built-in Gallery app. That means you can assign your own keywords and search for them later, much like you can on an iPhone. Depending on your Galaxy model and Gallery version, the exact location of the tagging controls may vary. However, Samsung supports manual photo tagging on compatible devices. Add tags to photos on Samsung Galaxy Here's how to tag a picture using Samsung Gallery. On some Galaxy versions, you may need to tap Edit in the photo's details to add a tag. If you don't see the option, make sure your Gallery app is updated. How to find tagged photos on Samsung Galaxy Once you've tagged a photo, you can use the Gallery's search feature to find it again. For example, you could tag pictures of your home appliances with their model names. Later, when you need a serial number or replacement part, you can search for the tag instead of scrolling through your entire camera roll. Create an album on Samsung Galaxy Albums offer another way to keep related pictures together, especially when you want to organize several photos from the same event or project. For example, you could create an album for home repairs and keep pictures of paint colors, appliance labels and receipts in one place. Pro tip: If you regularly photograph product labels or serial numbers, keep them together in an album called "Home information." You'll appreciate having those pictures handy when something breaks. HOW TO SAVE A VIDEO FRAME AS A PHOTO ON YOUR PHONE How to organize photos on Google Pixel Google Pixel phones take a different approach. Instead of relying on manually assigned keywords, Google Photos uses automatic recognition to help you find pictures based on what's in them. For example, you can search for "dog," "beach" or "receipt" and Google Photos may find relevant pictures without requiring you to tag them first. You can also create albums to organize pictures you want to keep together. How to find photos using Google Photos Google Photos can recognize many objects, places and other details in your pictures. Here's how to use its built-in search feature. Google Photos can often identify objects and locations without requiring you to manually label every picture. However, results depend on what the app can recognize, so you may need to try a different search term if your first attempt doesn't find the right photo. How to create albums on Google Pixel If you prefer organizing pictures yourself, albums offer a straightforward way to group related photos. To find your albums later, open Google Photos > Collections > Albums. You can create albums for vacations, family events or important household information. That way, pictures you frequently need are grouped together instead of scattered throughout your photo library. Find receipts and documents in Google Photos Google Photos also offers a useful feature for organizing certain documents automatically. On supported versions, backed-up pictures of receipts and other paperwork may appear in a dedicated Documents collection. To check, open Google Photos > Collections > Documents. If Google Photos recognizes documents in your backed-up pictures, you may find them organized into categories. This can be particularly helpful when you're trying to locate a receipt or another document you photographed months ago. Pro tip: Try searching Google Photos before creating dozens of albums. You may discover that it already recognizes much of what you're looking for. Smart ways to organize photos without wasting hours You don't need a complicated system to keep your pictures under control. In fact, a few consistent habits can make a bigger difference than spending hours organizing every image you've ever taken. Start with photos you know you'll need again. Travel confirmations and warranty information are good candidates. Then choose simple names that you'll remember when searching. Avoid overly specific labels that might be difficult to recall months later. For example, "kitchen repair" will probably be easier to remember than the exact date you photographed a broken dishwasher. Also, remember that photo organization doesn't replace a backup. Important pictures should be protected through a trusted cloud backup service or another reliable backup method. And if you're photographing sensitive information, think carefully about whether you want those pictures stored in a cloud account. STOP LOSING PHOTO QUALITY WHEN YOU SHARE PICTURES Kurt's key takeaways I've lost count of how many times I've taken a photo specifically so I wouldn't forget something, only to spend several minutes trying to find it later. A simple keyword or well-named album can solve a surprisingly annoying problem. What I like about Apple's approach is the ability to assign a word that means something to you. Your phone might recognize a picture of a car, but it doesn't necessarily know that you took it because you needed to remember where you parked. Samsung Galaxy users can take advantage of manual tags, too, while Google Pixel owners have powerful automatic search tools built into Google Photos. My advice is to start small. Organize the pictures you'll actually need again, and let your phone's built-in search handle the rest. Would you rather have your phone automatically analyze every picture to make it searchable, or would you prefer more control over how your personal photos are labeled and organized? articles.title: Dancing With The Stars Suspends Val Chmerkovskiy After 'Inappropriate' Social Media Post About Carrie Ann Inaba
articles.summary: Find out how long the pro will sit out the competition, and who'll partner Jenna Dewan in his absence.
articles.body:
One pro won't be "Dancing With the Stars" this week.

ABC has given a one-week suspension to Val Chmerkovskiy, the professional dancer who partners "The Rookie" star Jenna Dewan in the ABC competition's current season, TVLine has confirmed; he will not appear in the Tuesday, October 20 episode. Chmerkovskiy was yanked from the performance as a response to a social media post he made regarding judge Carrie Ann Inaba after the Oct. 13 episode.

In the post, Chmerkovskiy seemed to take issue with Inaba's criticism of a performance by his wife, fellow pro dancer Jenna Johnson, who partners "Grey's Anatomy" star Harry Shum Jr. "You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night," Chmerkovskiy posted to TikTok on Wednesday, seemingly referencing the 2022 Oscars telecast in which former "The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air" star Will Smith slapped host Chris Rock after Rock made a joke about Smith's wife, Jada Pinkett Smith. At the time, Will Smith also yelled to Rock that he should keep Jada Pinkett Smith's name "out your f***ing mouth."

"The well-being of everyone who works on 'Dancing with the Stars' is non-negotiable," BBC Studios, which produces the series, said in a statement. "Val's social media post was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show. As a result, he will not participate in next week's show."

Chmerkovskiy's TikTok later was deleted. Inaba posted about it to Instagram later in the week, and Chmerkovskiy made an Instagram story in which he apologized "from the bottom of my heart" for the post, adding that he'd reached out to Inaba to apologize.

"I should have never made the reference that I did and I deeply regret it," he wrote.

'In a moment where my instinct was to defend my wife, I made a poor decision'

On Saturday, Val Chmerkovskiy posted another Instagram story in light of his suspension.

"In a moment where my instinct was to defend my wife, I made a poor decision to reference a meme to 'keep my wife's name' out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention. Carrie Ann certainly didn't deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was."

He continued: "The last thing I want is to become a distraction from an important week or from the incredible work my dance partner Jenna Dewan is putting in. Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole DWTS family lots of love during Dedication Night. I'll be watching and cheering everyone on!!"

Alan Bersten, who partnered TV chef Giada De Laurentiis before she was eliminated earlier this season, will dance with Dewan in Chmerkovskiy's absence.

TVLine has reached out to Inaba for comment.

articles.title: The best gadget I bought this year is a milk frother
articles.summary: I bought a milk frother and I’ve been making fancy coffee drinks ever since.
articles.body: Back in February, I went to Los Angeles to take in some art and stayed in Koreatown. Down the street from my hotel, there was this little coffee shop — Stagger — that is, I think, best known for its matcha, which is good. But the drink I unexpectedly found myself obsessed with was their cream top, an iced Americano with, yep, vanilla cream on top. When I got back to Oakland, I kept thinking about how badly I wanted one. For more than 20 years, I’ve been drinking my coffee — iced or otherwise — black. Originally this was because I knew I could put black coffee that had cooled off in the microwave to reheat it without worrying that the milk in it would curdle. (Gross, I know.) Then, as I started drinking better coffee, it felt like the best way to appreciate the expensive beans I was buying. So my attachment to the cream top surprised me. And then, when Oakland had a gnarly heat wave in March, I decided there was one way I’d tolerate it: fancy coffee drinks. I splashed out $14 for the Zulay Kitchen frother and I was off. A handheld foamer looks and works kinda like an immersion blender. I pour milk into a glass, stick the frother in there, and then hold the power button until it reaches my preferred consistency. When the disposable batteries it uses are fresh, this takes about 30 seconds to a minute. As the batteries degrade, it takes longer; if I’m getting impatient about how long it’s taking me to make my frothy treats, it’s time to change the batteries. The frother also works to beat eggs, mix protein powder or creatine into a drink, and make hot chocolate. But by far it’s gotten the most use making my coffee drinks as I set out to make a cream top of my own. [Image: Also I think it’s neat to watch the foam descend into the coffee. The cream top descended from the Einspänner, an espresso drink that’s named for a one-horse carriage. The original Viennese version used hot espresso, and the whipped cream on top served as a kind of insulation, which kept the drivers’ drinks hot for them when they were out in the cold. (Obviously, its popularity expanded beyond carriage drivers.) It isn’t clear to me how the Einspänner made it to South Korea, but it exploded in popularity there, with all kinds of variations, mostly iced. And then from South Korea, it made its way to the US, where the ground had already been cleared by Starbucks’ “cold foam” drinks. The notable thing about the cream top, besides the addition of delicious fat and sugar to coffee, was that the cream wasn’t as light as latte foam, but wasn’t as heavy as ordinary whipped cream. It was melty and dripped slowly into the coffee. My first experiments with my at-home cream top were pretty simple. I don’t have an espresso machine, but I do make concentrated cold brew in hot weather, which has a strong enough flavor to stand up against the foam. (Some recipes suggest powdered espresso if you don’t want to use concentrated cold brew.) After I mastered the simple cream top, I began making forays into weirder breakfast treats, my favorite of which I… recreated from a Starbucks ad. It’s a cold brew with coconut ube cold foam, the top of which I dust with toasted coconut flakes. It is dank. (This is a recipe for a more sophisticated version than I make.) So when it was 90 degrees in Oakland for about two weeks running recently, this drink was how I consoled myself. To be honest, I’m just recommending getting a frother. You can spend a lot on a milk frother and some people do. I relied on America’s Test Kitchen to steer me in the right direction — but outlets like Wirecutter and Bon Appétit have their own preferred options. This one is cheap and simple, and it’s been treating me right. I’m sure the Apple HomeView is nice, too, but in pleasure per dollar can it match a $14 cold foamer that takes AA batteries? I have my doubts.

articles.title: Meet Ashley St. Clair, Elon Musk’s ex who claims he cut her child support from $100,000 to $20,000 after she rejected a $15 million NDA offer and publicly revealed their son
articles.summary: Ashley St.
articles.body: Ashley St. Clair, a former conservative influencer and author, has found herself at the centre of renewed attention following explosive claims about her relationship with Elon Musk in the new documentary Musk. Their online exchanges eventually developed into a relationship that she described as emotionally intimate.Recalling one of their early interactions, St. Clair said Musk responded to a Mother's Day post by encouraging her to have more children. She also recalled him telling her that she should have 10 children and suggesting that they have a child together.St. Clair has said Musk presented himself as a devoted father and appeared to maintain amicable relationships with the mothers of his other children.She later became pregnant and gave birth to Romulus in 2024. She publicly disclosed the birth in February 2025, bringing their relationship into the public eye.Ashley St. Clair’s claims about the NDA and child supportIn Musk, St. Clair alleges that she was offered $15 million upfront and $100,000 in monthly payments if she signed an NDA preventing her from discussing their relationship.She says she rejected the proposal because she did not want her son to grow up feeling that he was a secret.St. Clair claims Musk subsequently reduced her monthly payments to $40,000 and then to $20,000 after she publicly revealed the child's birth.Musk has disputed her account of the alleged agreement, reportedly stating on X that she was never offered the deal on the terms she described and accusing her of making false claims.The two have also been involved in a custody dispute over Romulus. She alleges that other women contacted her after interacting with the billionaire online and described conversations about having children with him.St. Clair also recalled an alleged text message in which Musk expressed a desire to have a “legion of children before the civil war”.Musk has publicly acknowledged having numerous children with different women. articles.title: ‘The Simpsons’ Surprise: Apu Is Heard for the First Time in Nearly a Decade, as Sunil Malhotra Takes Over for Hank Azaria (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the Oct. 18 episode of “The Simpsons,” “The Revengening,” which aired Sunday night on Fox. “The Simps...
articles.body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the Oct. 18 episode of "The Simpsons," "The Revengening," which aired Sunday night on Fox.

"The Simpsons" has pulled off its own October surprise: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon is back. The fan favorite character finally spoke again for the first time in nearly a decade on Sunday night's episode, "The Revengening." Variety has exclusively learned who is behind Apu's new voice: actor and voice-over vet Sunil Malhotra ("Grey's Anatomy," "The Legend of Korra").

Malhotra's hiring and the return of Apu — who has been seen, but not heard on "The Simpsons" since the October 2017 episode "The Serfsons" — was a closely guarded secret inside "The Simpsons" universe. Fox didn't share a screener for "The Revengening," and producers kept both the episode's table read and its subsequent production under tight protocols (including NDAs for all involved).

Also heard on Sunday's episode was the debut of Janina Gavankar ("The Morning Show") as Apu's wife, Manjula. And now that Apu is back and the Kwik-E-Mart has reopened, executive producer Matt Selman said both characters and the Nahasapeemapetilon family will once again be seen (and heard) on "The Simpsons" more often.

"We love this character, and wanted to bring him back in a smart, 'Simpsons'-y way that allowed him to evolve," Selman said. "We're excited by what Sunil has already brought to the role, and look forward to seeing more of Apu in the future."

Hank Azaria previously voiced Apu, a character that has been controversial over the years due to its stereotypical portrayal of a South Asian convenience store clerk. The issue of Apu was the centerpiece of the 2017 documentary "The Problem With Apu," in which comedian Hari Kondabolu discussed the impact the character has had on people of South Asian descent.

After that doc made waves — including in "The Simpsons" writers' room, where it was screened and discussed — Azaria announced that he would no longer voice Apu. "I apologize for my part in creating that and participating in that," Azaria said in 2021 on Dax Shepard's podcast "Armchair Expert." "Part of me feels like I need to go to every single Indian person in this country and personally apologize. And sometimes I do."

In the aftermath, Apu was shifted to the background on "The Simpsons," as producers decided how to handle the character going forward. For years, that meant Apu would still occasionally be seen in Springfield, but never heard.

Until now. The idea of bringing back Apu this way, as one of this year's Halloween-themed episodes, came from staffer Nick Dahan (who's the credited writer on "The Revengening") and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos. After hearing their pitch, Selman said he thought it was "a brilliant way" to bring Apu back and reference the entire situation.

Voice actor Malhotra said he took time to look into what it would mean to take over Apu and talked to the producers to make sure the character was more culturally appropriate.

"When my agent called me about a 'Simpsons' audition, I knew exactly what role it was for, and the idea actually made my stomach sink," he said. "But admittedly, part of me was also curious. It had been eight years since Apu had spoken on the show, and it got me thinking: Did the writers' room look different now? Could they bring him back in a way that acknowledged and apologized for past mistakes? Could I make the character my own, and reclaim him in some way? And could they achieve all of that in an unmistakably 'Simpsons' way that didn't disappoint fans?

"Whether the producers knew it or not, I was prepared to walk away," he continued. Malhotra said that he declined his very first "professional job offer 28 years ago" because it would have required him to play a stereotypical "Hindu guy," adding that playing such a caricature "to be the butt of the joke wasn't something I was willing to do, and I've turned down similar work multiple times since."

But as Malhotra got further down the road with "The Simpsons," he said, he began engaging with the producers about their plans for Apu before he would commit to the role, where he was promised that the return of Apu was being handled with the utmost care.

"My callback was the first of many times that no one at 'The Simpsons' let me down," he said. "I told casting that I'd only consider an offer if I could meet showrunner Matt Selman and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos, both of whom gladly did so. It was the beginning of a deeply collaborative experience that I hope is equally satisfying for longtime fans of 'The Simpsons' and for other South Asian kids who, like me, stopped watching at some point along the way."

In "The Revengening," a spooky lead-up to next week's "Treehouse of Horror XXXVII," a man in a "Daft Monk" Halloween costume (as in, a Daft Punk helmet and monastic robe — wordplay!) is accidentally killed over and over again by Springfield residents all over town. A year later, "Daft Monk" is still alive, and getting his revenge by taking out his would-be killers, one by one.

Eventually "Daft Monk" summons the townspeople to Springfield City Hall, where he takes his helmet off and reveals that he's actually Apu.

"I'd be lying if I didn't say that the sweetest part of all was unleashing that righteously rage-fueled "I AM APU!" — on behalf of so many of us — over and over in the studio until we got it just right," Malhotra said. "I really feel like we did and I can't wait for fans to see more Apu."

Apu then shares his backstory: After he was nearly killed dozens of times, he wound up on "The Island of Forgotten Garbage," where he's healed by "The Simpsons" quack Dr. Nick (who also has been seen sparingly in recent years). "All the junk Springfield gets rid of winds up here," he tells Apu, "like you … If you wound up here, it's for a reason, right, Leon?" (Out pops the character that Michael Jackson played in the Season 3 episode "Stark Raving Mad," which was pulled from "Simpsons" rotation in 2019 after the doc "Leaving Neverland" showcased more allegations against the late pop star.)

Says Apu before he reveals himself: "I am the man you left for dead. I am the one you pretended never existed!"

Then, unmasked, he tells the Springfield crowd: "It would have been so easy to bring me back. I immediately ran home to my family, but they were gone. Then I went to the Kwik-E-Mart, and was shocked to find it abandoned. As I wandered aimlessly through town, no one even noticed me. It was as if I was invisible. That was when I vowed to take my revenge on Springfield."

He's about to light City Hall on fire, but Marge Simpson pipes up — representing the Springfield citizens, but also clearly serving as a mouthpiece for the show's producers: "Apu, we're so sorry we left you for dead. Believe me, we wanted to do the right thing."

Bart adds: "But we were so scared, and just didn't know what to do."

Lenny also chimes in, in a nod to the debates inside "The Simpsons" writers' room: "If it's any consolation, we had so many internal conversations about it."

But, Carl finishes, "Ahh, they kind of just didn't go anywhere." (And for almost a decade, that's how "The Simpsons" never got around to bringing back Apu.)

Homer then offers to sacrifice himself to save the rest of the town, and offers this penance to Apu, while reminding viewers how important Apu has been to the makeup of Springfield: "I'm just doing what the old Apu would have done. The guy who loved this town and everyone in it. You were on our bowling teams, our barbershop quartets, our dad rock cover bands. We took you for granted. I took you for granted."

But before Apu can blow up the town, he wakes up. It turns out it was a nightmare; no one is dead. He's back in the Kwik E-Mart, and Manjula is there too. So is his No. 1 customer, Homer, who invites him to a Halloween party.

"What the heck? I'll do it," Apu says. "A Halloween party sounds kind of fun. Plus, I feel like I haven't seen everyone in ages. Oh, but I wish I had a costume."

But he actually does: There's a "Daft Monk" costume stashed under the cash register. So was it really a dream? And that's the end of the episode — but Apu is back!

This isn't the first time "The Simpsons" writers used their characters to allude to their indecisiveness on what to do with Apu. In the 2018 episode "No Good Read Goes Unpunished," Marge begins reading her favorite childhood novel to Lisa, but quickly realizes the old book was a lot more offensive and racist than she remembered. She tries to sanitize it, but "now it's as inoffensive as a Sunday in Cincinnati … what am I supposed to do?"

Lisa then looks at the audience, seemingly addressing "Simpsons" fans: "It's hard to say. Something that started decades ago and was applauded and inoffensive is now politically incorrect. What can you do?"

The scene pulls back to reveal a photo of Apu near Lisa's bed, and it's obvious they're no longer talking about a book, but their own show. With Marge also looking straight at viewers, the two suggest that "Some things will be dealt with at a later date … if at all." (It should be noted that Apu and his children also appeared in the episode, but did not speak.)

In June 2020, during the post-George Floyd reckoning on race, "The Simpsons" announced that moving forward, its characters of color would be voiced by culturally appropriate actors. Among the major changes, Alex Désert took over as Carl Carlson from Azaria, and Kevin Michael Richardson (who had already been a part of the series cast) became Dr. Julius Hibbert, which was previously Harry Shearer. Now, Apu, with Malhotra taking over, joins that list as well.

And for several years, the creative team promised that they would address Apu at some point. In 2021, series creator Matt Groening told USA Today that the producers were first seeing if they could make new Apu stories work. "I think the Apu stories are fantastic, and he's one of the most nuanced characters on a silly two-dimensional cartoon show," Groening said in the interview.

Early reactions on social media about the return of Apu has already been positive : "Apu is back thank you Simpsons," said one. Another : "The Simpsons reveals the new voice for Apu. Representation for Indian Americans. Well played Matt Groening and Dan Castellaneta, Hank Azaria, Nancy Cartwright, Harry Shearer, Julie Kavner and Yeardley Smith." Wrote a third: "Apu reveal is the greatest thing to happen on the Simpsons in a long time. I missed that genius character!"

Malhotra's recent voice credits include "The Legend of Vox Machina," "The Loud House," "Monster High," "The Casagrandes" and "Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi." He's also been heard on video games including "Mortal Kombat 1," "Avatar: The Last Airbender – Quest of Balance" and "Marvel's Avengers." In TV, besides "Grey's Anatomy," he's also appeared on "ER," "NCIS: New Orleans," "MacGyver" and "Maron."

articles.title: Abhishek Bajaj recalls playing football with Tiger Shroff moments before firing incident, says ‘We were playing together, he is safe now’
articles.summary: Actor Abhishek Bajaj has spoken about the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff, reassuring fans that the actor is safe.
articles.body: Actor Abhishek Bajaj has spoken about the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff, reassuring fans that the actor is safe. Abhishek was present at the football ground where the incident reportedly took place and revealed thatthey had been playing together before the firing occurred.Speaking to News18 Showsha, Abhishek said, “Yes, we were playing together before the incident happened. We are fine. He’s safe now. No need to worry at all.”Shots were reportedly fired near Pushpa Park in Juhu, Mumbai, where Tiger Shroff had gone to play football. According to reports, the actor’s driver, identified as Firdaus, sustained an injury to his left hand and was admitted to a hospital for treatment.Following the incident, concerns grew over Tiger’s safety. Jackie Shroff’s team subsequently reassured everyone about the actor’s well-being, stating, “Tiger is okay. Thank you so much.”Following the firing, reports emerged claiming that Lawrence Bishnoi and members of his gang had taken responsibility for the attack. A social media post allegedly shared by gangster Anil Pandit on behalf of Lawrence Bishnoi also surfaced.However, the authenticity of the alleged claim and the motive behind the firing have not been officially established. As reported by India Today, the claim remained unverified while the investigation continued. Mumbai Police are investigating the incident and searching for the accused to establish the circumstances surrounding the firing.Meanwhile, a video allegedly showing the moments surrounding the incident has surfaced on Reddit and circulated on social media.
